inspectedText: The scholar-authored reference identifies the Crafts' public 1848 escape: Ellen dressed as a southern slaveholder and William as her valet, passing through trains and steamers to Philadelphia. It explains the later Boston refuge and threat under the 1850 Fugitive Slave Act, leading to England. It explicitly distinguishes sole title-page attribution to William from later scholarship on Ellen's role in shaping the memoir. The bibliography points to historical and literary research rather than proving every reconstructed conversation.
